findings.title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The PR replaces the Lithuanian translation of `totpStep1` (which previously contained HTML anchors and therefore failed the new HTML verification) with the sentence "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:". That sentence is Italian, not Lithuanian — it was apparently copied from the wrong locale's message file. Users running the account console with the Lithuanian locale will see Italian instructions on the multi-factor authentication setup page. It should be a Lithuanian rendering of the English source "Install one of the following applications on your mobile:".

findings.title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: Same defect as in the account theme: the Lithuanian `loginTotpStep1` value was replaced with "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Users with the Lithuanian locale will see Italian instructions on the OTP setup page of the login flow. It should be a Lithuanian translation of the English source "Install one of the following applications on your mobile:".

findings.title: Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) file now contains Traditional Chinese text
findings.body: The new value of `totpStep1` in the zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) account bundle is "在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：", which is written in Traditional Chinese characters (手機/安裝/應用程式 instead of 手机/安装/应用程序). The rest of the file, and the zh_CN locale generally, uses Simplified Chinese — compare the neighboring lines such as `totpStep2=打开应用扫描二维码输入验证码`. The string looks like it was pasted from a Traditional Chinese (zh_TW) source; it should use Simplified characters for consistency with the locale.

findings.title: Anchor-mismatch error message does not say which key or file is affected
findings.body: When a translation contains an anchor tag that does not match the English source, `santizeAnchors` records the message `Didn't find anchor tag <a ...> in original string` with no message key and no file path — even though the `key` parameter is passed to the method and `file` is available as a field. Every other diagnostic produced by this class (duplicate keys, illegal HTML) includes the file and the key. When the plugin scans the entire themes tree, this message gives maintainers no way to locate the offending entry without grepping all message bundles for the anchor text. Include `key` and `file` in the message.

findings.title: Anchor check enforces identical anchor order, not just identical anchors
findings.body: `santizeAnchors` walks the anchors of the translation and of the English value with two independent matchers and requires them to be equal pair-by-pair in sequence (`Objects.equals(matcher.group(), englishMatcher.group())`). This enforces that anchors appear in the same ORDER as in the English source, not merely that the same set of anchors is present. A legitimate translation that reorders two links because the target language has different word order will fail verification with "Didn't find anchor tag", blocking valid translations. Consider matching anchors as a multiset (e.g., remove each matched anchor from a list of English anchors) instead of pairwise by position.
